name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. A scenic hill station at about 1,500 m elevation with colonial architecture, lakes, parks, markets, and access to surrounding waterfalls and viewpoints.
facts: Headquarters of East Khasi Hills district
Named after the deity U Shyllong
Popular base for exploring Khasi Hills

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, located roughly 10 km south of Shillong. Offers panoramic views of the city, surrounding hills, and distant plains on clear days. Sacred to the Khasi people as the abode of U Lei Shillong.
facts: Requires ID for entry due to nearby installations
Popular for sunrise and sunset views

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Cascades over moss-covered rocks amid dense ferns and greenery, about 12 km from the city centre on the road toward Sohra.
facts: Originally named for a rock resembling an elephant
Easy access with stairs to viewing points

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: India’s tallest plunge waterfall at 340 m, plunging from the Sohra plateau into a turquoise pool. Located near Rangjyrteh village about 5-7 km from Sohra town, fed by plateau rainfall and associated with a local Khasi legend.
facts: Plunge pool has distinctive green hue
Named after the legend of Ka Likai

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Historic town on the southern edge of the Khasi Hills plateau, once recorded as the wettest place on Earth. Base for exploring waterfalls, caves, living root bridges, and viewpoints overlooking Bangladesh plains. Local name is Sohra.
facts: Gateway to Nohkalikai and living root bridges

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented waterfall about 315 m high near Mawsmai village, appearing as seven parallel streams during monsoon. Cascades over limestone cliffs on the Sohra plateau edge, offering dramatic views especially in the rainy season.
facts: Best viewed during monsoon for full flow

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Limestone show cave near Sohra with illuminated stalactites and stalagmites. One of the first caves developed for tourism in Meghalaya, offering a short, accessible underground experience amid the wettest region.
facts: Length of visitor section around 150-250 m

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, grown from Ficus elastica roots guided by Khasi people over generations. Requires a steep descent of about 3,000-3,500 steps from Tyrna; one of the most famous bio-engineered structures in the world.
facts: Trek of roughly 3500 steps from Tyrna
Lower bridge estimated over 180 years old

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Cleanest village in Asia award-winning community in the Pynursla block, known for its immaculate streets, living root bridges, skywalk viewpoint over Bangladesh plains, and matrilineal Khasi culture. About 80-90 km from Shillong near the India-Bangladesh border.
facts: Declared cleanest village in Asia in 2003
Features living root bridges and viewpoints

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon and viewpoint near Smit village, about 25 km from Shillong. Offers sweeping vistas of endless green hills, deep valleys, and traditional villages; the name means ‘end of the hills’ or ‘endless hills’ in Khasi.
facts: Name translates to endless or end of hills
Popular for trekking and panoramic views

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove (Law Lyngdoh) near Mawphlang village, about 25 km southwest of Shillong. Protected for centuries by Khasi tradition as the abode of deities; rich in biodiversity, old trees, monoliths, and forbidden to remove anything from the forest.

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Major cultural museum in Mawlai, Shillong, showcasing the indigenous peoples, traditions, artefacts, and lifestyles of Northeast India. One of the largest and most informative museums dedicated to the region’s tribal heritage.
facts: Also known as Don Bosco Museum
